html:
SMTO-SKL-0155 — Your saved GitHub account details aren't filled in correctly

GUID: 7cf6f28b-9e7a-5e23-b2a2-2bcbb2ed703a
Slug: github-account-invalid
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • SMTO found your saved GitHub account, but some of its details are missing or in a form SMTO can't use. It didn't contact GitHub.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, select your GitHub account entry, open the Value tab and select Reveal & edit value. The problem is in the saved details, and this is where you can see and change them.
  2. Check the account ID is a plain number without quotes. You can find it by opening api.github.com/users/ followed by your GitHub login in a browser and copying the id. SMTO needs the number GitHub uses for your user, not your login name or an organization's number.
  3. Check the credential type is fine_grained_pat or classic_pat, the token has no spaces, and the authorized repositories list has at least one entry written as owner/name. Then select Save. Each of these must be in the expected form before SMTO will use the account.
  4. If it still won't save cleanly, create a fresh entry from the GitHub Account template and copy your details into it without adding or removing fields. The template has exactly the fields SMTO expects.

What success looks like

  • When you ask SMTO to check your GitHub connection, it shows your GitHub login as verified.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't send your token; the copied details don't include it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The GitHub Account profile failed validation: wrong profile_type, non-integer profile_version or account_id, or fields that do not match the supported schema (credential_type, token format, authorized_repositories, granted_permissions).

What this means

  • Account profile has the wrong type or fails exact integer version/account-ID and supported schema validation. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • Account profile has the wrong type or fails exact integer version/account-ID and supported schema validation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect typed profile fields, PAT type and explicit repository allowlist without revealing the token.

How to fix it

  • parameter_profiles.validate rejects the record when profile_type is not github_account, profile_version/account_id are not integers, or the value fails the strict schema (all fields required, no extra fields, credential_type fine_grained_pat or classic_pat, token of letters/digits/underscore, at least one owner/repo in authorized_repositories, granted_permissions using supported keys with none/read/write). Correct the profile in the Parameter Store editor or recreate it from the GitHub Account template.
  • Correct the GitHub Account profile fields, explicit repository allowlist and supported PAT credential type in Parameter Store.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended account validates through the supported profile editor.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
